raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.name: Graduation Proximity
raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.description: Students closer to graduation generally receive greater priority, particularly when delaying the requested course could delay graduation.

raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.name: Degree Progress
raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.description: Students with fewer remaining credit hours generally receive greater consideration.

raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.name: Course Requirement
raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.description: Required courses generally receive greater priority, although electives may also be urgent.

raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.name: Course Availability
raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.description: Courses offered less frequently generally receive greater priority, particularly when the next expected offering is after graduation.

raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.name: Previous Attempts
raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.description: Students who have never attempted the requested course receive greater consideration on this factor.

raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.name: Prerequisite Completion
raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.description: Confirmed unsatisfied prerequisites generally justify LOW priority. Unresolved or conflicting evidence may require MANUAL_REVIEW.

raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.name: Academic Progression
raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.description: Courses affecting remaining required courses generally receive greater priority. Dependency counts alone must not determine priority.

raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.name: Evidence Quality
raise_capacity_prioritization_rules.description: Missing or conflicting critical evidence that prevents a reliable assessment requires MANUAL_REVIEW.

priority_levels.HIGH: Delaying the course presents a significant risk to timely graduation.
priority_levels.MEDIUM: Delaying the course could affect academic progression but is unlikely to delay graduation.
priority_levels.LOW: The course can reasonably be delayed without significant academic impact, or verified academic circumstances justify lower priority.
priority_levels.MANUAL_REVIEW: Insufficient or conflicting evidence prevents a reliable assessment.
